nodes.title: Organizational Behavior
nodes.description: This course discusses individual attitudes and behavior within organizational contexts, processes such as perception, learning and motivation; group processes; leadership, organizational culture, organizational change and the effects of societal culture on work-related attitudes.

nodes.title: Research Methods and Statistics for Psychology II
nodes.description: This course continues to develop students' understanding of, and competence in, study design and data analysis. It emphasises the use of more sophisticated techniques to test more complex predictions involving multiple predictors.
nodes.prereq_text: SPS 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and PSY 202 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Experimental Psychology
nodes.description: This course gives students practica experience in designing, conducting, analysing and reporting psychology experiments, in small groups. The emphasis will be on encouraging students to analyse design decisions, to minimise the influence of confounding variables, and to maximise power. The course will also give a thorough grounding in scientific writing and appropriate reporting format.
nodes.prereq_text: SPS 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and PSY 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and PSY 202 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Testing and Measurement
nodes.description: This course provides the students with necessary skills to measure psychological constructs as well as knowledge on test construction, validity and reliability issues. It also covers topics such as factor analysis and administration and scoring procedures of various types of tests, including standardized tests of intelligence.
nodes.prereq_text: PSY 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and SPS 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D (can be taken concurrently) and PSY 202 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Emotion
nodes.description: This course will introduce students to the rapidly developing field of emotion science. Students will learn about the biological function, neurology, and physiology of emotions in humans and other animals, and about strategies for measuring and classifying emotions. The course will also examine interactions between emotion and cognitive functions, and how these can be used to understand and treat mental illnesses.
nodes.prereq_text: PSY 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and SPS 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Sensation / Perception
nodes.description: This course will cover basic principles of sensation and perception in vision, audition and other modalities by mainly focusing on the structure and the function of the sensory systems, which will be discussed in terms of how information is processed. Additionally, some of the following questions will be discussed in this course. What are the anatomical structures of the senses? What are the factors which has an effect on these complex processes? How does the perception arise from information gathered by the sensory system?
nodes.prereq_text: PSY 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and SPS 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Language
nodes.description: This course provides an overview of research on the psychology of language. Students will be exposed to a wide range of topics including language acquisition in infancy and childhood, second language learning, the neural processing of language, and language education. The course equips students with theoretical and methodological understanding of research on language and mind.
nodes.prereq_text: PSY 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and SPS 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Memory
nodes.description: This course will provide the students with an overview to the scientific study of human memory. Topics that are covered include, but not limited to, memory systems and processes; such as encoding, forgetting; memory disorders and developmental approaches. Everyday applications of memory will also be explored.
nodes.prereq_text: PSY 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and SPS 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and PSY 310 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Applied Social Psychology
nodes.description: This course offers a social psychological perspective on how to help individuals become happy, healthy, wise, and nice. It will use cutting-edge research and theories in social psychology to develop strategies, policies, and business ideas that improve individual happiness and health, encourage wise decisions in organizational and educational settings, and promote prosocial behavior.
nodes.prereq_text: PSY 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and SPS 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Abnormal Behavior
nodes.description: Theories and approaches to understanding psychopathology and treatment to, and prevention of abnormal behavior. Emphasis is on current theory, research, issues in, and the role of clinical psychology in contemporary society.
nodes.prereq_text: PSY 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and SPS 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Personality
nodes.description: This course aims to introduce students to different approaches in personality, such as, psychodynamic, cognitive, social learning, and trait approaches, and provide the background to evaluate and critique them.
nodes.prereq_text: PSY 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D and SPS 102 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D

nodes.title: Child and Adolescent Psychopathology
nodes.description: This course provides a scientfic and theoretical basis for understanding specific disorders of childhood and adolescence. Topics to be covered include the clinical symptoms, assessment procedures, prevalence, etiology and treatment approaches of the most commonly diagnosed disorders.

nodes.title: Psychology of the Self
nodes.description: This course aims to present an overview of the recent theories and research in the self literature. The course also covers how self and attachment processes interact and their cultural implications. Particular emphasis is placed on the formation and nature of self- development, self-esteem, self-regulation and attachment.

nodes.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
nodes.description: Cognitive neuroscience is a branch of neuroscience which studies processes of nervous system underpinning cognitive functions (acquisition, storage, transformation, and use of knowledge). The course explores the neural mechanisms underlying cognitive processes such as perception, attention, memory, and decision- making. In light of behavioral and neuroimaging research, the course aims to deliver the skills to interpret cognitive neuroscience research and understand human cognition.
nodes.prereq_text: PSY 201 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D or PSY 310 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D or PSY 350 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D
